subject: Embeddings endpoint latency spike after catalog update — urgent
snippet: Customer reports p95/p99 regression on embeddings after catalog change; team coordinated rollback and temporary routing; follow-up postmortem scheduled.
messages:
From: Miguel Sanchez <miguel.sanchez@acme-corp.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Acme AI Platform Team <api-platform@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T09:12:34-07:00
Subject: Sudden spike in embeddings latency after catalog push

Hi Jonas + Redwood team,

We started seeing a sharp increase in embeddings latency right around 08:50 PDT this morning — p95 and p99 are both jumping 2-3x compared to our baseline. This coincides with the model catalog update noted in the release notes (it references switching the default variant for embedding-compact-v2).

Impact: our nightly enrichment pipeline is missing SLAs (jobs are timing out) and search relevance updates are delayed. Attached is a Datadog screenshot showing the p95/p99 curves (datadog_acme_embed_latency_20260712.png).

Sample request ids: see attachment acme_sample_ids_20260712.txt.

Can you confirm whether the catalog change affected routing for our account or if there's a broader runtime issue? We need an ETA—this is impacting revenue-facing jobs. If you need to escalate, please loop in execs.

Thanks,
Miguel
Platform Engineer, Acme Corp

--
Attachment: datadog_acme_embed_latency_20260712.png (image/png)
Attachment: acme_sample_ids_20260712.txt (text/plain)

From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Miguel Sanchez <miguel.sanchez@acme-corp.com>
Cc: diego_fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T09:25:10-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden spike in embeddings latency after catalog push

Thanks for the quick flag, Miguel — really sorry for the disruption. I'm looping in Diego and Rishi to triage, and Evelyn from CS so we can coordinate customer communications.

Immediate ask from our side: can you confirm whether these sample IDs are all hitting the embeddings route or if some are batched requests? Also, do you have a short window (15m) where the team can run additional traces?

We're investigating two immediate mitigations: 1) pinning your account routing to the previous model variant (non-disruptive config change), or 2) rolling back the catalog change more broadly if we see it's causing regressions across customers. Before taking company-wide action, we'd prefer a targeted fix for Acme to minimize blast radius.

Diego — can you look at KV cache metrics and variant selection logs around 08:45-09:05?

I'll keep you posted every 20 minutes.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: rollback_runbook_jonas_20260712.md (text/markdown)

From: diego_fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Miguel Sanchez <miguel.sanchez@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T09:37:58-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden spike in embeddings latency after catalog push

Quick findings from the runtime side (initial):
- We see a correlated increase in KV-cache miss rate starting 08:48 PDT for requests routed to embedding-compact-v2.
- There are a handful of requests triggering a fallback execution path that forces FP32 kernels rather than the optimized quantized path — that increases per-token latency significantly under load.
- Batch sizes for Acme's traffic changed slightly due to client-side batching adjustments, which amplifies the latency impact when the execution path falls back.

I've attached a short profiler dump with example traces (profiler_dump_diego_20260712.txt). Miguel: the sample IDs you provided map to the traces in the dump — see trace ids T-23A/T-23B.

Next steps I'm executing now:
1) Push an account-scoped routing override to pin Acme to the pre-update variant (embedding-compact-v1) — low risk and reversible.
2) If that brings p95 back down, we keep the override and run a deeper root-cause to understand why quantized path regressed for compact-v2.
3) If override doesn't work, we'll prepare a catalog rollback and coordinate a maintenance window.

I'll post status in 15m.

- Diego
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

--
Attachment: profiler_dump_diego_20260712.txt (text/plain)

From: Miguel Sanchez <miguel.sanchez@acme-corp.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme AI Platform Team <api-platform@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T09:45:04-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden spike in embeddings latency after catalog push

Thanks Diego — confirmed the sample IDs map to the traces you referenced (T-23A/T-23B). Most of our nighttime enrichment jobs are batched between 09:30–10:15 PDT; if latency stays high through that window we'll miss multiple deadlines.

If this isn't resolved within the next ~3 hours we will need to escalate to our engineering leadership and potentially shift back to our internal temporary embedding store. Please keep us posted on the rollback plan and any ETA.

-Miguel

--
Attachment: acme_sample_ids_20260712.txt (text/plain)

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: diego_fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Miguel Sanchez <miguel.sanchez@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T10:02:21-07:00
Subject: Urgent: proposed mitigation for Acme routing (requires quick approval)

Evelyn — looping you in since this is customer-impacting and Acme is asking for exec visibility if unresolved.

Proposal (technical owner: Laura):
- Immediate: apply an account-scoped routing override to route Acme traffic back to embedding-compact-v1. This is a config change in the routing plane and should be reversible without downtime. Estimated time to apply: 10 minutes.
- Short-term: run a targeted canary of compact-v2 with tightened resource allocations and monitor KV cache behavior.
- Post-incident: add a regression test to model-catalog deployment that validates quantized kernel paths under representative batch sizes.

Jonas — please confirm you have Acme approval for the account-scoped change so Laura can apply it. If Acme prefers a full catalog rollback we'll schedule that but it requires broader comms.

I'll standby for confirmation to proceed.

Thanks,
Rishi
Engineering Manager, Runtime Reliability

--
No attachments

From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Miguel Sanchez <miguel.sanchez@acme-corp.com>, Acme AI Platform Team <api-platform@acme-corp.com>
Cc: diego_fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T10:18:07-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden spike in embeddings latency after catalog push

Miguel — we have your verbal okay to proceed with the account-scoped routing override and have executed the change at 10:12 PDT. Early metrics show p95 improving (see updated Datadog view: https://app.datadoghq.com/graph/embed?from=162&to=172&view=acme-embeds-p95).

What we did:
- Pinned Acme traffic to embedding-compact-v1 via account routing override (non-disruptive).
- Spun up a targeted canary pool for compact-v2 with increased cache warming to replicate your traffic pattern.

Preliminary results: p95 dropped ~40% within 5 minutes of the override; throughput returned to expected levels. We're keeping the override in place while Diego and Laura run a deeper RCA.

Next steps:
- 30-minute postmortem with your team at 14:00 PDT today to walk through root cause and long-term fixes. I'll send a calendar invite.
- Postmortem doc and action items will be shared within 24 hours.

Apologies again for the disruption — we'll treat this as a high-priority reliability issue and update you every hour until resolved. Please reply if you still see client-side errors.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: rollback_runbook_jonas_20260712.md (text/markdown)
